newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares stall in shock at Wall Street twist.
newsitem.headline: German shares stall in shock at Wall Street twist.

text.p: Wall Street's surprising overnight about-turn after an early surge shocked the German share market into early losses Wednesday and left it trapped in a narrow range throughout a markedly cautious floor session.

The 30-share DAX index, catching up with a surge in late electronic dealings Tuesday, ended 9.87 points higher than Tuesday's mid-afternoon close at 2,999.20, but was down some 29 points from Tuesday's closing level on the IBIS DAX, which also tracks post-bourse dealings.
March DTB DAX futures were down 27 points at 3,016.

"It was definitely a shock to see the Dow Jones ending lower after being up 100 points," said one dealer of Wall Street's reverse on Tuesday after initially surging on the back of a lower-than-expected fourth quarter labour cost report.
Dealers said volumes were thin, with investors loath to make a move until key U.S. data -- durable goods -- were released in the early afternoon.
"It's a complete toss-up where we go next. The forecasts for durable goods are all over the place," another dealer said.
Chemical shares, which were overlooked in a recent switch to exporters, were the strongest blue chip sector.
BASF AG, trading heavily, advanced 80 pfennigs to 59.90 marks while Bayer AG rose 75 pfennigs to 62.30 marks.
Commerzbank AG extended its decline after Tuesday's below-forecast earnings report for 1996 to end down 50 pfennigs at 41.90 marks.
